about.summary: Object-oriented software for model-robust covariance matrix estimators. Starting out from the basic robust Eicker-Huber-White sandwich covariance methods include: heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC) covariances for cross-section data; heteroscedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent (HAC) covariances for time series data (such as Andrews' kernel HAC, Newey-West, and WEAVE estimators); clustered covariances (one-way and multi-way); panel and panel-corrected covariances; outer-product-of-gradients covariances; and (clustered) bootstrap covariances. All methods are applicable to (generalized) linear model objects fitted by lm() and glm() but can also be adapted to other classes through S3 methods. Details can be found in Zeileis et al. (2020) <doi:10.18637/jss.v095.i01>, Zeileis (2004) <doi:10.18637/jss.v011.i10> and Zeileis (2006) <doi:10.18637/jss.v016.i09>.

name: r-sandwich
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set version = "3.1-2" %}
{% set posix = 'm2-' if win else '' %}

package:
  name: r-sandwich
  version: "{{ version|replace("-", "_") }}"

source:
  url:
    - {{ cran_mirror }}/src/contrib/sandwich_{{ version }}.tar.gz
    - {{ cran_mirror }}/src/contrib/Archive/sandwich/sandwich_{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: d096fe24aba3f118f82ea2ac7c5d607dcdf2926c2c76fcf97ae14c81d4b58161

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: generic
  rpaths:
    - lib/R/lib/
    - lib/
  missing_dso_whitelist:
    - '*/R.dll'        # [win]
    - '*/Rblas.dll'    # [win]
    - '*/Rlapack.dll'  # [win]

requirements:
  build:
    - {{ posix }}zip               # [win]
    - cross-r-base {{ r_base }}    # [build_platform != target_platform]
  host:
    - r-base
    - r-zoo
  run:
    - r-base
    - r-zoo

test:
  commands:
    - $R -e "library('sandwich')"           # [not win]
    - "\"%R%\" -e \"library('sandwich')\""  # [win]

about:
  home: https://sandwich.R-Forge.R-project.org/
  license: GPL-2.0-or-later
  summary: 'Object-oriented software for model-robust covariance matrix estimators. Starting
    out from the basic robust Eicker-Huber-White sandwich covariance methods include:
    heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC) covariances for cross-section data; heteroscedasticity-
    and autocorrelation-consistent (HAC) covariances for time series data (such as Andrews''
    kernel HAC, Newey-West, and WEAVE estimators); clustered covariances (one-way and
    multi-way); panel and panel-corrected covariances; outer-product-of-gradients covariances;
    and (clustered) bootstrap covariances. All methods are applicable to (generalized)
    linear model objects fitted by lm() and glm() but can also be adapted to other classes
    through S3 methods. Details can be found in Zeileis et al. (2020) <doi:10.18637/jss.v095.i01>,
    Zeileis (2004) <doi:10.18637/jss.v011.i10> and Zeileis (2006) <doi:10.18637/jss.v016.i09>.'
  license_family: GPL3
  license_file:
    - '{{ environ["PREFIX"] }}/lib/R/share/licenses/GPL-2'
    - '{{ environ["PREFIX"] }}/lib/R/share/licenses/GPL-3'

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - conda-forge/r
